g.title: in
g.text: is the package whose DEPEND / RDEPEND / BDEPEND / PDEPEND we are reading, because it is itself being planned;
that dependency names. All atoms for that one child are grouped into a single request.
The proof context carries: the parent's identity, a slot lock, the versions already chosen in this proof, and learned ranges

g.title: s1
g.text: as the parent, and the request is for runtime:
the parent will provide it itself once merged, so it is satisfied by definition
memberchk(self(Repo://Parent), Ctx), Parent has C/N, Action = run

g.title: vocab
g.text: the package being planned whose dependency list names the child
: "the package this proof step is about")
the dependency asks for; we must pick a version of it
one concrete version of the child, taken from the tree
(an ebuild depending on itself, e.g. a bootstrap compiler)

g.title: aug
g.text: Tighten the request with the parent's own RDEPEND bounds
install-time requests only: if the parent's RDEPEND
names this child with a version range,
add that range to the request now, so we do not pick a child version the parent will reject at runtime

g.title: s2
g.text: 2 · Does an installed copy of the child already do the job?
same slot, every version bound holds, required USE flags are built in
(PDEPEND ignores USE drift), and no rebuild was requested

g.title: r2
g.text: Keep the installed copy, nothing to merge

g.title: s3
g.text: 3 · Pick a version of the child from the tree
enumerate candidates newest first, check each against every rule,
work out the USE flags it must be built with, decide install vs update vs downgrade

g.title: r3
g.text: the proof gains: the chosen entry and its action, "this C/N is now fixed to this version" (selected_cn),
the version range this edge demands (cn_domain), and the USE flags it must be built with

g.title: guard
g.text: Is it safe to learn from this failure?
not when the failure is a USE/REQUIRED_USE clash already recorded, and not when a
shared provider is about to be rebuilt with a forced USE flag (that rebuild may fix it)

g.title: s4
g.text: 4 · Was it a wildcard range we can learn as a hard bound?
"=pkg-6.31*" becomes a learned range [6.31, 6.32) for this package, if the parent
has only one version or was already narrowed (otherwise step 5 goes first)

g.title: s8
g.text: 8 · Give up on this dependency, but say why
the proof continues with an assumption that carries the reason (nothing in the tree,
no version fits, impossible USE, slot conflict) and the best suggestion

g.title: s5
g.text: 5 · Blame the parent: this version of the parent asks for something no child version can give
reject exactly this parent version, so the retry picks the next parent version (which may ask for something else).
Not done when: the request is PDEPEND, a slot we have not met yet, the child itself
can be re-chosen instead, the only problem is visibility, or the parent is what the user asked for

g.title: retry
g.text: Prover restarts the pass with the new knowledge

g.title: s6
g.text: 6 · Blame an earlier choice: the version of the child already chosen for another parent does not fit this one
reject that chosen child version (or the package whose blocker introduced the conflict) and retry

g.title: s7
g.text: 7 · Is the only problem that every version is hidden?
masked by the profile, or not keyworded for this architecture

g.title: r7
g.text: Plan it anyway, with a suggestion
rerun step 3 while pretending the mask / keyword rule is relaxed for this one dependency,
remember that this entry may pass its own visibility check, tag "unmask" or "accept keyword"
